clue.text: Truth from lady with Florence perhaps

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name, a typical crossword 'lady'
Florence is an example of a city, the Italian one, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Someone seeks the truth from a woman who is with her friend Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Florence' reads as a second woman's name beside 'lady', but it is the Italian city, standing for any city.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity is a formal synonym for truthfulness or accuracy.

clue.text: Six approaching Chaldean city go in force

indicators.note: in signals that the word go is placed inside the joined pieces

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
Ur was the ancient city of the Chaldees in Mesopotamia
taken as written

explanation.surface: Six people approach an ancient city to enter by force.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur of the Chaldees is the biblical city, a favourite crossword source for UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy, strength and vitality are what forcefulness means.

clue.text: Periodical survey

definitions.meaning: a magazine published at intervals, often critical
survey as a verb or noun, a general look over

explanation.definitionFit: Both a magazine of critical essays and an assessment or inspection.

clue.text: Remove faults? That's right

definitions.meaning: to put mistakes right, mark work

explanation.surface: A question about fixing mistakes, answered by saying that is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for amending errors and an adjective for accurate.

clue.text: Notables are becoming treacherous

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so these letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Distinguished people are turning into traitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is treason, so the adjective means traitorous.

clue.text: Outlaw group reaching city centre

parts.note: a band is a group of people, musicians or otherwise

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letters of the word city

explanation.surface: A gang of outlaws arrives in the heart of town.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living outside the law, a synonym for outlaw.

clue.text: Pleas to remove evangelist

indicators.note: remove read as re-move, shift around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Appeals are made to get rid of a preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of Christ's twelve disciples spread the gospel, an early missionary.

clue.text: Explain one second-class screed being written about

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the other pieces
being written suggests being rewritten, so the letters of screed are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
B is a second-class grade, after A

explanation.surface: Explaining a second-rate long rant someone is composing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being written' rearranges SCREED into DESCRE, and 'about' puts IB inside it after DESCR.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an account in words of something, setting out what it is like.

clue.text: Refuse to go lower

definitions.meaning: to reduce a setting, such as volume or heat

explanation.surface: Someone declines to drop their price.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a phrasal verb for rejecting and for lowering a dial or flame.

clue.text: Did some ruling

parts.note: read plainly it suggests drawing lines with a ruler or a judge's decisions; really it means exercised authority over a country

explanation.definitionFit: To rule a state is to control and direct it, the past tense of exercising power.

clue.text: Cat right to follow timid person

indicators.note: the letter for right is told to come after the timid person, so it goes at the end

parts.note: a shy, timid person is called a mouse

explanation.surface: A cat is right to chase after a timid little creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' looks set to be the hunter in the scene; it is the definition, a cat that catches mice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat kept to catch rodents is named for its prey, the hunter of small vermin.

clue.text: Vain plea from conservationists

definitions.meaning: vain here means futile, achieving nothing
an appeal to consume fewer resources, split as two words

explanation.surface: Green campaigners' appeals to cut consumption are said to be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile and without purpose; and, split in two, an appeal to consume less, the sort of slogan environmentalists use.

clue.text: Admitted having come onto the stage

definitions.meaning: admitted in the sense of let in, allowed through the door
an actor making an entrance from the wings

explanation.surface: An actor confessed to something after walking on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let in and an actor walking on are both the past tense of going in.

clue.text: Two ladies with one characteristic of part of the 16th century

definitions.text: characteristic of part of the 16th century

parts.note: Eliza is a woman's name
Beth is another woman's name
an is the indefinite article meaning one

explanation.surface: Two women share a trait from the 1500s.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Elizabeth I reigned from 1558, so the latter part of the 1500s bears her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the reign of Elizabeth I, the Tudor era of Shakespeare.

clue.text: Problem at the joint for racketeer?

definitions.text: Problem at the joint for racketeer?

parts.words: Problem at the joint for racketeer?
parts.note: a racketeer sounds like a gangster with trouble at a criminal 'joint'; really it is a player wielding a racket with an aching arm joint

explanation.definitionFit: A painful inflamed tendon at the outside of the arm's hinge, common among racket-sport players.

clue.text: Separated detail so confused

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specific point is cut off so it becomes muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Set apart from others, alone and cut off.

clue.text: Piece of cloth fellows found inside measure

indicators.note: found inside means the cloth and fellows are placed within the measure

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for feet or foot, a measure
a rag is a piece of cloth
men are fellows

explanation.surface: A scrap of fabric that some men have discovered inside a measuring container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cloth' looks like one unit for RAG; 'Piece' alone is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken-off part or fragment of a whole is a bit or shard.

clue.text: Jumping-off place

parts.note: literally a flexible board divers leap from; figuratively a starting point for a venture

explanation.definitionFit: A diving board launches a jumper, and figuratively any platform for a new start.

clue.text: How footballer might be making clear profit

definitions.text: How footballer might be making clear profit

parts.words: How footballer might be making clear profit
parts.note: a footballer scoring puts the ball into the net; a business clearing a profit after costs is doing the same verb

explanation.definitionFit: Scoring a goal into the mesh, and earning a sum after deductions.

clue.text: Warrant served in error to head engineer

indicators.note: to head says the rearranged letters come before the engineer's letter
in error means wrongly arranged, so the letters of served are rearranged

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for engineer or engineering

explanation.surface: A warrant was served on the wrong person, then went to the chief engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges SERVED into DESERV; 'to head' puts that before E.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit or be worthy of something, as a verb.

clue.text: Criticise strike when on strike

parts.note: to hit is to strike
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A union boss denounces a strike while members walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack verbally, lash out with harsh words.

clue.text: Take up strategic positions from French manoeuvre

parts.note: de is the French word for from
a ploy is a cunning manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Troops take position after a French tactical move.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread troops or resources out into position for action.

clue.text: Willing beneficiary?

parts.note: willing seems to mean eager, but it means being left something in a will

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inherits a bequest under a will receives a legacy.

clue.text: Forming a unit in French train

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a train of attendants is a suite, a retinue

explanation.surface: Something fitting together as a whole inside a French railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests a railway; it is a retinue of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathroom attached to a bedroom, or rooms joined as a set, are together as one.

clue.text: This cockney man's included dissertation

indicators.note: included signals that the cockney phrase is placed within the word this

parts.note: taken as written
'he's' in a cockney accent drops its H, giving 'es

explanation.surface: A Londoner's contribution is part of an academic paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech famously drops the H, so 'he's' becomes 'ES; 'included' places it after TH in THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A long piece of academic writing submitted for a degree is a synonym for a dissertation.

clue.text: Burn one fuel to get another

parts.note: to char is to scorch or burn
coal is one kind of fuel

explanation.surface: Burning one kind of fuel produces a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another fuel: the clue is nearly all-in-one, since charring wood makes this fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Charred wood is itself burnt as a fuel, a different one from coal.

clue.text: Dorothy to get on with blind love

parts.note: Dot is a short form of the name Dorothy
to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: Dorothy grows older alongside an unseeing sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides old age, the word has an older sense of foolish, doting affection, which 'blind love' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of the word is excessive, uncritical fondness, doting on someone.

clue.text: A new church's attempt at family tree

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England, and the possessive 's adds an S
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A new church makes an attempt at drawing up a genealogy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage and forebears, the line of descent a genealogy chart shows.
